original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.

scope_change_reason: The card asks for one explicit alphabet extension with its implementation charged. Refined to the pair-source connector call family B_jk: z += B_j x_j + B_k x_k on the pinned five-source universal-connector-boundary model: one complete query per pair call, charged two coefficient/source accesses, no other interface change.
actual_scope: Add exactly one operation family (pair-source connector calls B_jk) to the fixed single-source connector alphabet and determine the exact minimum universal source path and exact complete-query optimum for the five-source all-31-nonzero-row matrix in the extended alphabet, priced against the predecessor's fixture.
bottleneck_link: The connector batch's complete queries are recursive-interface boundary work: the fixed alphabet's optimum 74 sat above the 72-query support bound which that alphabet proves unattainable. The pair family changes exactly this boundary cost: 74 -> 72, support bound attained.
stop_rule: Stop when the exact minimum source path is pinned (construction plus exhaustive nine-point census), one fully priced comparison against the predecessor fixture is recorded, and the dirty replay and controls pass. No search beyond length 10 and no second alphabet family in this session.
evidence: verify.py: word with D(w)=F2^5 by two recomputations, dirty replay at L=1,2,3 with seeded dense nonsymmetric noncommuting maps and exact boundary on all 31 outputs, three mutation controls rejected, exact pricing numbers; verify.py --full: independent itertools census of all 7,888,725 nine-point sets (0 covering, maximum coverage 29) excluding length 9.
author: Aaron Wang

open_questions.question: Do triple-source calls B_jkl lower the five-source universal path below ten, and at what leaf price?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Each added source per call raises leaf cost but could shorten the path; the prefix-set method answers it exactly and would locate the family-size optimum.
open_questions.first_step: Repeat the closed-walk census with steps of Hamming weight up to 3 (25 step types) at lengths 8 and 9, with the same counting lower bound.
open_questions.blocked_by: Nothing structural; it is a bounded enumeration, though larger than the weight-1/2 scan.

open_questions.question: What is the pair-call universal path minimum for six sources?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The predecessor stops at the five-source boundary; six sources test whether the pair family scales or the covering sets become walkable only at large length.
open_questions.first_step: Establish the counting bound (|P| >= 12 since C(11,2) = 55 < 63 <= C(12,2)) and run a walkwise search at lengths 12 and 13 on F_2^6.
open_questions.blocked_by: The setwise census grows to C(63,11); a walkwise or meet-in-the-middle search is required instead.

open_questions.question: How does a real compiler price a pair-source call's second coefficient access inside one query record?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The 72-query result assumes a pair call is one dispatch record with two coefficient/source accesses; the break-even against the fixed alphabet depends on that price.
open_questions.first_step: Instantiate one pair call in the universal-connector-boundary tape implementation sketch and count its instruction records and coefficient reads.
open_questions.blocked_by: The predecessor leaves common-label realization open even for single calls; this inherits that blocker.
